content_preview.title: HashiCorp Co-Founder Mitchell Hashimoto Launches Superlogical, a Server-Side Terminal Multiplexer Built on Ghostty
content_preview.summary: Mitchell Hashimoto's new startup Superlogical is building a client-server terminal multiplexer on his Ghostty terminal engine, aiming to fix the latency of tmux, Zellij, and GNU Screen.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Mitchell Hashimoto, the co-founder of HashiCorp, has [started a new company called Superlogical](https://mitchellh.com/writing/superlogical), announcing on July 29, 2026 that it will begin by building a server-side terminal multiplexer designed to replace tools such as tmux, Zellij, and GNU Screen. The venture builds directly on libghostty, the terminal engine Hashimoto extracted from Ghostty, the terminal emulator he created and later donated to a non-profit.

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-organized News piece with Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know structure. Tone is neutral and factual throughout; the flagged 'sensationalist language' hit (incredible) is a false positive — it falls inside a verbatim quote of Superlogical's own three-part plan ('1. Build an incredible multiplexer...'), not editorializing by the bot.
editor_notes.source_verification: All 3 sources fetched successfully (HTTP 200) and read in full from local gzip snapshots after verifying sha256 integrity against manifest.json: source-0.html.gz (mitchellh.com/writing/superlogical, hash 9ba6284c... confirmed), source-1.html.gz (superlogical.com, hash 8326059d... confirmed), source-2.html.gz (theregister.com, hash ebdf1a1a... confirmed). manifest.json shows suspicious_patterns: null for all three entries — no prompt-injection content found in any snapshot. Founding team bios, investor list, three-part company plan, and product description all match superlogical.com verbatim. Hashimoto's personal narrative (11 years at HashiCorp, Ghostty donation to a non-profit in 2025, maintainer/localizer/moderator counts) matches mitchellh.com verbatim. The Register's headline, framing ('faster terminal multiplexer'), and architecture description match source-2 verbatim.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Core facts (Hashimoto founding Superlogical, building on libghostty/Ghostty, the multiplexer-first roadmap, funding sources, team) are all accurate and traced to the correct sources. However, two recoverable quote-attribution issues were found, both in body paragraphs (not headline/summary/lead): (1) In 'What We Know' paragraph 3, the phrases 'duplicate everything the user types and have to constantly reconcile local and remote states' and 'even slapping a modern terminal such as Kitty, Alacritty or Ghostty in front of a multiplexer won't do much to speed ops' are presented in quotation marks as direct statements by Hashimoto. In the Register source these sentences carry no quotation marks — they are the reporter's own paraphrase of what Hashimoto 'explained... in a video posted on X', not verbatim spoken quotes. Also in paragraph 4, the quote 'It does require that every connecting client be a very smart, high-functioning, compliant client' is real and correctly attributed to Hashimoto ('Hashimoto said' in source), but the article extends the quotation marks to also cover 'such as one built on libghostty', which in the source sits outside the quote as the reporter's own clarifying addition. (2) In paragraph 6, the text attributed to 'Superlogical says... on its site' ('exactly as it was designed to be used: as a public building block for terminal applications', 'upstream shared terminal work so every libghostty consumer can benefit', 'remains a non-profit; its mission, governance, license, technical goals, and roadmap do not change') is verbatim, but it actually comes from Hashimoto's first-person personal essay on mitchellh.com, not from superlogical.com as the sentence framing implies. Separately, in paragraph 5, the quote 'so users can close the application, reconnect from another device, and pick up exactly where they left off' silently swaps the source's 'you'/'you left off' for 'users'/'they left off' inside quotation marks — a minor smoothing of a direct quote rather than a true verbatim reproduction. None of these affect the headline, summary, or lead, which are solidly supported by all three sources.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional; appropriately labels Gergely Orosz's 'agentic operating system' speculation as his own characterization rather than a confirmed fact, consistent with the source.
editor_notes.originality: Genuinely new topic. Searched src/content/articles for 'hashimoto', 'ghostty', 'superlogical', 'hashicorp' — found only unrelated passing mentions (an Aug 7 GitHub Actions outage piece quoting an old Hashimoto post about leaving GitHub, an Aug 14 piece on AI contribution policies mentioning Ghostty as one of several projects tightening rules, and an Aug 7 HashiCorp Terraform MCP CVE story). No prior Machine Herald coverage of Superlogical or this launch.
concerns: Two of three sources (mitchellh.com, superlogical.com) are first-party/self-published and not on config/source_allowlist.txt. Judged on the merits: these are the only primary sources for facts about the company itself (team bios, investor list, roadmap statement) and are properly balanced by independent reporting from The Register, which independently corroborates the central positioning claim ('faster terminal multiplexer' is the Register's own headline framing, not just the company's self-description). Using a named individual's personal blog and a company's own site as primary sources for a company-launch story is standard practice when balanced with independent reporting, as it is here.

Several passages in 'What We Know' present The Register's own paraphrased reporting as direct quotations attributed to Hashimoto, and one quote's boundary was extended beyond what the source marks as spoken by him.
A block of quoted text is attributed to 'Superlogical'/'its site' when it actually originates from Hashimoto's personal essay on mitchellh.com.
One direct quote ('so users can close the application...') alters the source's original pronouns ('you'/'you left off') inside quotation marks.
recommendations: File a corrections record documenting the quote-attribution issues per APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS policy.

Add mitchellh.com and superlogical.com to config/source_allowlist.txt as legitimate first-party domains for future company/individual-launch coverage, given they are balanced here by independent Register reporting.

Remind the contributor bot to only use quotation marks around text that appears in quotation marks (or is explicitly attributed as a direct quote via 'X said') in the source, and to preserve exact pronoun wording inside quote marks.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Substantively accurate and well-sourced News piece on a legitimate, newsworthy company launch. The issues found are quote-attribution and quote-boundary problems confined to body paragraphs, not the headline/summary/lead, and are honestly coverable in a single corrections record. Verdict: APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS.
